editorial:
Imagine being a scared eight-year-old kid in 1986 Madras who accidentally locks the city's most dangerous gangster in a gross school bathroom. That is exactly how this wild ride starts. You get this great mix of tension and laughs as the big, tough criminal realizes he is stuck and totally dependent on a little boy for food and help. The vibe feels like a time machine, taking you back to old-school India with bright colors and a story that feels both sweet and stressful at the same time.

The acting is what really sells it, especially the chemistry between the kid and the thug. You will love how the gangster slowly softens up, though the action scenes still pack a punch when things get chaotic. While the middle part slows down a bit, the emotional payoff is totally worth it.
endingExplained: In the end, the gangster's crew finally finds him, but he refuses to go back to his old life of crime. He chooses to protect the boy from his own gang in a final big fight. After the dust settles, he disappears from the city to start over. The movie closes with a flash-forward showing the boy as an adult, revealing that the gangster secretly funded his education, proving their bond lasted a lifetime.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves odd-couple friendships and stories set in the past.
